title: How I know when my app breaks: not more testing, Sentry.
hook: Your app breaks. Who tells you?
summary: Sentry error tracking: how I know when my app breaks, not more testing.
body: Sentry error tracking: how I know when my app breaks, not more testing.

Tests check your code once, before it ships. Nothing checks it once it's live. Sentry does: when I stopped a project on Vercel it flagged "this website is no longer reachable", and it caught the globe in Atlaria not loading for people.
I'm Manraj Sidhu, AI developer, and this is the real build.

Setup is five steps: run the wizard, add an uptime monitor, send alerts to Slack or email, upload source maps, throw a test error. Save this before you ship again.
Which dev myth would you call out? "Just test it more" is mine.

Comment SENTRY and I'll send you the link.
Follow @manrajtalks for more of The Stack.
guide: Add error tracking to your app so you hear about breakages before your users do. You need a deployed web app (for example on Vercel) and a free Sentry account.
1. Create a free account at Sentry and add a new project for your app's framework (for example Next.js).
1. Install the Sentry SDK in your app by following the setup steps Sentry shows for that framework.
1. Add the project's DSN (the key Sentry gives you) as an environment variable in your host, such as Vercel, then redeploy.
1. Trigger a test error on purpose and check that it appears in the Sentry Issues list.
1. Add an uptime monitor in Sentry for your site's URL, so you are alerted when it stops responding.
1. Set up email alerts for new issues and for the uptime monitor.
1. Break something deliberately, such as pausing the project on Vercel, and confirm the "site not reachable" alert arrives.

Watch out: testing alone will not tell you whether your app works for real people, so confirm alerts actually reach you before you rely on them, and never publish your DSN-linked environment variables in public code.
